newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Activity picked up on the South African bond market on Tuesday as London and New York players returned from a holiday and the first of a slew of economic figures due this week hit the market.
But the forex market remained mostly lacklustre with the rand patroling a tight 4.4650 to 4.4800 band, holding up well in the face of on-going -- albeit small-scale -- dollar demand.

At 1618 GMT the government's benchmark R150 loan yielded 14.98 percent from 15.04 percent late on Monday after the market managed to break through the (15 percent) figure before lunch as local institutions bought stock.
"There was good demand and supply and I would say the market is in equilibrium," a senior trader at a big institution said.
He said there had been two-way trade from most counter parties with foreigners and jobbers both buying and selling stock.
The April private credit extension figure, due out at 1500 GMT on Wednesday, was seen as the next key number, together with the money supply release.
A Reuters consensus of 10 analysts called for credit growth to rise to 16.40 percent year-on-year from 15.96 percent previously.
Money supply was seen climbing to 16.70 percent from a preliminary 16.39 percent.
Also due on Wednesday is the April inflation rate at 0900 GMT and the market will be watching out for the release of first quarter GDP growth figures at 0730 GMT on Thursday.
Bond traders said there had been a fair amount of volume around the 14.95 area where investors had turned sellers.
The market was seen holding Tuesday's 14.95 to 15.03 percent range on Wednesday ahead of the money supply and credit data.
"If the market goes to 14.94 it will be seen as a selling opportunity and if it breaks 14.92 on the downside that changes the whole scenario again," commented a second trader.
Lower U.S. Treasuries, where the U.S. 30-year long bond hit seven percent during the day and was last trading at 7.04 percent, were seen weighing on the market.
Foreigners were net buyers of 47.61 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Monday after selling 338.10 million rand's worth on Friday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal turnover on the exchange was 4.42 billion rand on Monday from 5.52 billion rand on Friday.
At 1430 GMT the rand was at 4.4755/4785 against the U.S. dollar, slightly weaker from Monday's late level of 4.4710/4740.
Forex traders said the unit had held in a narrow range although there was continued upward pressure towards the 4.48 level.
"London guys bought dollars and the central bank pushed it lower again," one commented.

Another said the bank was determined not to let the rand weaken past the 4.48 level but there were a lot of dollar buyers lurking around and the rand could test the higher 4.4950 level over the next two to three weeks.
In cross rate action, the rand was last little moved at 0.3798/3802 to the mark from 0.3775/3779 late on Monday.
The local unit was changing hands at 26.0106/0392 yen from 26.0170/0456 yen previously and 7.2892/2986 rand to the British pound from 7.3293/3387 before.
South Africa's money market shortage rose to 7.599 billion rand on Monday from 6.700 billion rand on Saturday, the Reserve Bank said.
Three-month NCD rates remained unchanged from Friday at 16.35 percent offered, as did 90-day BA rates which lined up at 15.85 percent.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482-1003
